patch_resolves_note: The fixed line adds the missing `dist_from_out_buf_start == 0` rejection to the non-wrapping back-reference guard. In the fixed original run the PoC remains clean and only the guard event executes, with no downstream back-reference copy or Adler32 scan event.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code statement that materializes the attacker-controlled compressed buffer and its exact length inside miniz's `mz_stream` state before any inflate logic runs.

The non-wrapping back-reference guard checks only `dist > dist_from_out_buf_start`. On the witnessed path both values are 0, so the predicate is false and tinfl falls through into the copy even though no initialized output bytes exist yet.

Repo-source sink block for the saved MSan crash. In `common_exit`, this Adler32 recomputation walks the produced output bytes; on the witnessed path `buf_len` is 32, so its reads consume the prefix just populated from uninitialized heap data.
The regular back-reference copy uses pSrc equal to pOut_buf_start, so the copy reads from the output buffer base itself.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records backref_copy.copy_src == backref_copy.output_base == 0x70f000000000.

edges.description: The same dist_from_out_buf_start value computed at the non-wrapping guard becomes the prior_output_len used by the regular back-reference copy.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records nonwrapping_guard.dist_from_out_buf_start == backref_copy.prior_output_len == 0.

edges.description: The output buffer base involved in the regular back-reference copy is the same base pointer later scanned by the Adler32 sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records backref_copy.output_base == adler32_scan.buf_base == 0x70f000000000.
